title: Filter through an asynchronous data source without showing stale results
problem: Once rows come from an asynchronous source, each filter keystroke can start a request. Responses arrive in any order, and a component that renders whatever arrives last will show results for a filter the user has already changed. The loading, empty and failed cases then collapse into one blank table.
context: Builds on the sortable table. The caller now supplies a data source function that takes the current query and returns a promise of rows.
impact: This is the state model the whole component depends on. An error here produces tables that are wrong in ways nobody notices, which is worse than tables that visibly fail.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The design states which state the component owns (query, sort, load status, rows) and which the caller owns, and every state transition is listed.
A response for a superseded request is never rendered, whatever order responses arrive in.
Loading, empty, error and populated are distinct states, both visually and programmatically. An error is never shown as an empty table.
After an error the controls remain usable and a retry reissues the current request.
A polite live region announces the result count after a filter or sort settles, not on every keystroke.
Automated tests use a controllable fake data source to resolve responses out of order and to reject, and cover every listed transition. All pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains how staleness is detected, one rejected alternative, and what happens to an in-flight request when the component is removed from the page.

constraints: The component itself uses no runtime dependencies. TypeScript, a test runner and a DOM implementation for tests are the only development dependencies.
No state management library. Timing in tests is controlled by the test, not by real timers or sleeps.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: Component state, its transitions, and the asynchronous boundary.

investigation_areas: Which request is current, and what makes that knowable when a response arrives
Whether debouncing solves staleness or only makes it rarer
How to make asynchronous ordering deterministic inside a test
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
documentation_requirements: Record the state ownership table and transition list in the learner design.
